macro.headline: Soft CPI ignites relief bid, but tape is uneven under the surface.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY sits at $749.17, above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, in an established uptrend with MACD above signal and RSI at 54.7 — constructive but not extended. QQQ, by contrast, has slipped below its 50-day, RSI 47.8, MACD bearish, sitting below the middle Bollinger band; the Nasdaq 100 read is materially weaker than the S&P. The Dow (+5.2% over 21 days) and Russell 2000 (+4.2% over 21 days) are outperforming QQQ (+2.7%), a classic broadening/rotation signature. VIX is 17.5, up 8.6% over 5 days but still down 9.9% on the month; the VIX3M/VIX ratio remains in contango. WTI oil surged +13.7% over 5 days to $80.10, while gold (-2.7% / 5d) and silver (-4.5% / 5d) are trending down under a DXY that is still above its 50-day. The 10Y yield is 4.61%, up on the week, and the 2s10s spread widened sharply (+14.3% over 5 days) — a bear-steepener move.

The tracked conversation leans firmly bullish and attributes the tone almost entirely to today's CPI print: June headline CPI 3.5% vs. 3.8% expected, core 2.6% vs. 2.8%, described as the largest monthly decline since April 2020. The dominant view is that this collapses July FOMC hike odds to ~8%, which is being framed as the release valve for the equity bid — chart reads highlight S&P futures rallying into the print. A parallel bullish thread points to IBM, KOSPI, STOXX50E and refiner/agriculture names (VLO, ADM) as broadening leadership beyond mega-cap tech. The bearish minority focuses on AAPL and SPY hedging via UVXY, and the tracked conversation also flags an IBM earnings collapse (~-20% intraday on software/infrastructure weakness) and a fresh oil bid tied to Iran-related supply concerns. This partially aligns with the data — a soft-CPI narrative is consistent with 2s10s steepening and the Dow/Russell outperformance — but conflicts with the QQQ break of its 50-day and the bearish MACD in Technology. Sentiment is telling a broadening story; the tape is confirming that only outside of large-cap tech.

Sector rotation supports the broadening thesis: Financials (score 9.2, RSI 67.9), Healthcare (8.8), Utilities (8.8), Consumer Staples (8.5), and Energy (8.2) are all HOT with bullish MACD. Technology (score 4.2, RSI 47.9, MACD bearish) and Materials (2.8) are the laggards. The rotation radar surfaces validated Early-Runway industries in Diagnostics & Research, Health Information Services, Credit Services, Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing, and Travel Services — all still early in their hot spells (typically 12–18% through a median run) with top-decile cross-sectional RS. This is where the validated rotation tailwind lives today.

Forward watch: the CPI-driven bid needs the QQQ to reclaim its 50-day and the 10Y to stop backing up to confirm a durable trend leg. Oil above $80 is a wildcard — bullish for Energy longs, but a re-acceleration in crude would undermine the disinflation story the sentiment is trading. Watch VIX 5-day trend; another leg above 20 would cap this macro read.
